parties:
Zauz Ali Molla ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Fatema Bibi and others ----- Opposite parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of one of the heirs of the deceased plaintiffs is directed against an order of the learned Munsif refusing, to make the preliminary decree final on the ground that the application was made after a long lapse of 43 years. The learned Munsif, however, noticed an order dated 16.4.31 striking off the suit for non-compliance of certain order of the Court. 

 2. At this stage there is no dispute that one Mariam Bibi instituted Title Suit No. 788 of 1929 in the 2nd Court of Munsif at Bagerhat for partition and the said suit was decreed in preliminary form on contest on 31.7.30 granting the plaintiff 6 minas 15 gondas share in the property in suit. There is nothing on record to indicate that the said preliminary decree was varied or altered on appeal or review, Meanwhile, Title Suit No. 41 of 1973 has been instituted by the ooposite party Nos. 3 to 6 for declaration of their title to some land of the aforesaid partition Suit No. 788 of 1929. During the pendency of the said suit, the heirs of Mariam Bibi filed a petition for final decree in terms of the preliminary decree. The learned Munsif however, rejected the petition mainly on the ground that the order dated 16.4.31 was not challenged by the persons effected thereby and that it was filed after a long lapse of 43 years by the heirs of the original plaintiff Who cannot maintain the petition for final decree. 

 3. Mr. Nizamuddin Haider, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule contends that the suit was decreed in preliminary form granting certain shares in favour of the plaintiff and as such the suit was not liable to be dismissed unless the said preliminary decree was reversed on appeal. In support of this proposition, Mr. Haider has referred to the case of Laehmi Narain Marwary and others Vs. Balmakund Marwary and another 29 C.W.N. 391. In this case their Lordships of the Privy Council held that an order dismissing the suit after the preliminary decree was passed was without jurisdiction. In the instant case the order dated 16.4.31 is an order by which the said suit was struck of for non-compliance of the Court's order relating to commissioner's fee, etc. An order of this type has been described by their Lordships of the Privy Council as "unfortunate" order. This appears to consonance with the principle that decree passed by the Court in preliminary form remains pending until the final decree is passed. Evidently, the said partition suit did not reach up to the stage of the final decree because of non-compliance of certain order. Their Lore ships of the Privy Council did not approve ail order of the type of the instant case. Although it was noticed that negligence or dilatoriness on the part of the parties might create some obstruction, nevertheless it was not intended that such a suit could be struck off during the stage of the final decree. 

 Similar view is available in the case of Kambala Sundararajamma Vs. P. S. Ramuln Chetty and others A.I.R. 1932 Madras 519. In this case it has been held that "after a preliminary decree in a partition suit has been Passed it is not competent to the Court to dismiss the suit subsequently. The preliminary decree can only be reversed on appeal and whatever default there may be in the subsequent stages of the suit, that preliminary decree itself cannot be vacated." Similar view is also available in the case of Lachmi Narayan Tewari and others Vs. Ramsaran Tewary and another A.I.R. 1925 Patna 433. In this case it has been held that "the Court has no jurisdiction to dismiss the suit after a preliminary decree has been passed in a partition suit merely because, there has been delay in producing the commissioner's fee. Keeping the above principles in view, it is evident that the learned Munsif failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in him in not allowing further proceeding of the said partition suit, the object whereof is attainment of final decree through Court. The grounds as to the lapse of time and the order dated 16.4.31 do not appear to stand on sound footing. Evidently the order dated 16.4.31 was without jurisdiction. The lapse of 43 years is of no consequence in a suit for partition where a preliminary decree was lawfully granted by a Court. 

 4. Mr. M. A. Sattar, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties has pressed his contention that long lapse of time and absence of any action on the part of the person effected by the order dated 16.4.31 rendered the preliminary decree incapable of further proceeding towards the final decree. Mr. Sattar is not supported by any authority in respect of his contention.
